::: {.cite-bar .domain-defense-arms}
[In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Pub. L. 81-216]{.cite} [63 Stat. 578]{.cite} [10 U.S.C. 111, 151]{.cite}
:::

Fixed the weak structure created in 1947. It turned the National Military Establishment into the Department of Defense, an executive department, and reduced the Army, Navy, and Air Force to military departments under the Secretary of Defense.

## Key provisions

- Created the Department of Defense as an executive department.
- Removed the service secretaries from the cabinet and from the National Security Council.
- Created the position of Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, without command authority.
- Added a deputy secretary and comptroller and gave the Secretary control of the budget.

## Why it matters

It is the first of three corrections to the [National Security Act](nsa-1947.qmd), followed by the [DoD Reorganization Act (1958)](dod-reorg-1958.qmd) and the [Goldwater-Nichols Act](goldwater-nichols-1986.qmd), each of which moved authority from the services toward the Secretary and joint commanders.

## Current status

In force as carried into Title 10 and revised by the 1958 and 1986 reorganizations.
